_metadata: Plain-language rewriting judge suite (plain_language_v1, 5 passages). Each row gives a dense/bureaucratic passage to rewrite for a general audience; scored by the LLM-as-judge against the reference using tasks/rubrics/plain_language_v1.yaml. Originals are illustrative Duke-flavored phrasings and references are hand-written PLACEHOLDER golds (not validated by a Duke communications/compliance office) — pipeline validation, not authoritative. New questions go in a new version file.

question: Rewrite the following in plain language for a general student audience, keeping all the facts: "Students must remit payment of all outstanding account balances prior to the commencement of the registration period; failure to do so will result in the placement of a financial hold precluding enrollment."
reference: Pay off any money you owe on your student account before registration opens. If you don't, you'll get a financial hold and won't be able to register.

question: Rewrite this IT instruction in plain language, keeping the steps: "To remediate the authentication failure, users should purge cached credentials from the operating system keychain and subsequently re-establish the multi-factor enrollment via the designated self-service portal."
reference: If you can't sign in, first delete your saved Duke password from your computer's keychain (its saved-password store). Then set up multi-factor authentication again using the self-service portal.

question: Rewrite this notice in plain language for students, keeping the deadline and consequence: "Submission of the enrollment verification form is required no later than the fourteenth (14th) calendar day of the semester; non-submission will render the student ineligible for the associated tuition adjustment."
reference: Turn in your enrollment verification form within the first 14 days of the semester. If you miss that deadline, you won't qualify for the tuition adjustment.

question: Rewrite this research-consent sentence in plain language, keeping the meaning: "Participation in this study is wholly voluntary, and the participant may elect to withdraw consent at any juncture without incurring any penalty or forfeiture of benefits to which they are otherwise entitled."
reference: Taking part in this study is completely your choice. You can stop at any time, and you won't lose any benefits you would normally get.

question: Rewrite this financial-aid clause in plain language for a general audience, keeping the condition: "Continued eligibility for need-based aid is contingent upon the maintenance of satisfactory academic progress as defined by the institution's published standards."
reference: To keep getting need-based aid, you have to keep making satisfactory academic progress, which the school defines in its published standards.
